title: Nepali Congress Faces Internal Division Ahead of Convention - ABC NEWS NEPAL
description: Nepali Congress Faces Internal Division Ahead of Convention  ABC NEWS NEPAL
publisher.title: ABC NEWS NEPAL
full_article:
Kathmandu— Nepal’s Nepali Congress (NC) is experiencing significant internal strife following last year’s Gen Z movement and subsequent general elections, which signaled public dissatisfaction with existing governance. The party, historically a key agent of change in the country, now finds itself deeply divided between an establishment faction led by Gagan Kumar Thapa and an anti-establishment group headed by former president Sher Bahadur Deuba, who are contesting the legitimacy of the current leadership and control over the upcoming 15th general convention scheduled for October 2026.

The Role of Political Parties

A strong relationship exists between political parties and democratic systems; parties thrive within democracies and are essential to their function. Throughout history, they have often led struggles against autocratic regimes in favor of establishing democratic governance, providing citizens with platforms for advocating freedom, equality, and human rights. In a functioning democracy, these parties serve as vital links between the government and the populace, earning votes based on performance both in power and opposition.

Electoral Discontent and Party Response

Last year’s protests led by Gen Z highlighted issues of bad governance, corruption, political syndicates, and unemployment, contributing to a desire for change reflected in recent elections. While the electorate sought new leadership through these polls, electoral losses have triggered internal rifts within some parties, particularly Nepali Congress. The party has struggled to institutionalize past achievements and deliver tangible improvements to citizens’ lives, leading to recurring unrest.

Leadership Dispute Intensifies

The current division within NC stems from a disagreement over the legitimacy of a Special Convention that elected Gagan Kumar Thapa as president; Sher Bahadur Deuba's faction contests its validity. A Supreme Court review petition filed by Deuba and Purna Bahadur Khadka has further fueled the conflict, with the anti-establishment group anticipating a reversal of the court’s recognition of the Thapa-led central working committee. Both factions are now at odds over control of the 15th general convention.

Calls for Unity

Supporters of the Special Convention maintain it reflects public demand for reform and generational leadership change, claiming over half of party representatives backed the move. Despite the deep divisions, voices within the party advocate for unity, emphasizing that strong and unified parties are essential to fulfilling promises made to the electorate. Reconciliation and finding common ground between the factions are seen as crucial steps forward.

The future direction of Nepali Congress remains uncertain as the dispute over leadership continues, with both sides awaiting a potential ruling from the Supreme Court that could reshape the party’s structure and influence its upcoming convention.

(With inputs from RN)

नेकां के भीतर वर्तमान विभाजन एकटा विशेष अधिवेशन के वैधता पर असहमति स उपजल अछि जाहि में गगन कुमार थापा के अध्यक्ष चुनल गेल छल; शेर बहादुर देउबा के गुट एकर वैधता के मुकाबला करैत अछि । देउबा आरू पूर्णबहादुर खड्का द्वारा दायर सुप्रीम कोर्ट केरऽ समीक्षा याचिका न॑ द्वंद्व क॑ आरू तेज करी देल॑ छै, जेकरा म॑ संस्थापन विरोधी समूह न॑ थापा नेतृत्व वाला केन्द्रीय कार्यसमिति क॑ कोर्ट केरऽ मान्यता उलटै के उम्मीद करी रहलऽ छै । आब 15म आम अधिवेशन पर नियंत्रण पर दुनू गुट मे विवाद अछि।

title: Nepal-India Border Dispute: Meetings Yield No Decision on Lipulekh - Ratopati
description: Nepal-India Border Dispute: Meetings Yield No Decision on Lipulekh  Ratopati
publisher.title: Ratopati
full_article:
Kathmandu. Since the formation of the government under Prime Minister Balendra Shah, two main joint meetings have been held with India regarding border issues.

The meeting of the Nepal-India Survey Officials Committee was held on July 29 in Lucknow, India, and the meeting of the Joint Working Group on Border Management was held on August 4 in Dehradun, India. Attention was focused on these two important meetings amidst the ongoing border dispute between Nepal and India.

However, neither of these meetings made any decision on the issue of Lipulekh, Limpiyadhura, and Kalapani. Due to the unresolved problem of this land, which has been disputed for a long time, conflicts always escalate between the two countries on the border issue. Although it is said to be resolved through diplomatic talks, no concrete initiative has been found from anywhere so far for a solution.

The meeting of the Survey Officials Committee held on July 29 agreed to survey the land claimed to be encroached by each other between Nepal and India. After Prime Minister Balendra Shah expressed that not only India has encroached on Nepal's land but Nepal has also encroached on India's land, an agreement was reached to investigate the land that both countries have been occupying.

After the Prime Minister's statement, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs also issued a statement clarifying that due to the adoption of certain border principles in riverine areas during the determination of the Nepal-India border, 'cross-border occupation' has occurred, leading to a situation where citizens of one country cultivate and reside on land within the territory of the other country.

Although both countries agreed to study those lands and resolve the dispute, nothing has been said about Lipulekh, which is the biggest dispute. An official from the Survey Department, who participated in the meeting, said that the committee was not even given the mandate (authority) to study or discuss Lipulekh. He informed that during the two-day meeting held in India, neither side even discussed this issue.

According to him, Lipulekh is a very sensitive issue, and it cannot be resolved without high-level intervention. He stated that lower-level employees do not want to take risks regarding the disputed Lipulekh. He warned that if this is not resolved soon, it could take a more serious turn, saying, 'We cannot say that another mess won't happen there tomorrow, so it is better to resolve it as soon as possible.'

This too ‘The Lipulekh dispute is not technical, it must be resolved politically and diplomatically’

Dehradun Meeting

In the meeting of the Joint Working Group held in Dehradun on August 4 and 5, although Lipulekh was informally raised, it was stated that it was not discussed as an agenda item. Instead, the working group decided to increase surveillance and strictness on the Nepal-India border.

This too Strict surveillance will be carried out on the Nepal-India border

The meeting discussed facilitating cross-border movement of citizens of both countries, increasing surveillance of third-country nationals, disaster management, and repair of damaged border pillars. However, no decision was made on Lipulekh, Limpiyadhura, and Kalapani.

According to border scholar Ratna Bhandari, the Lipulekh dispute has now become a political dispute between the two countries. He states that because it is being used as a political tool, no one is showing interest in resolving it. He said, 'Specifically, India does not want to resolve it, and Nepal has also not shown sufficient interest, which is why the dispute has not been resolved so far.'

Bhandari stated that during the India-China war in 1962 (1966 according to the text), India placed its army there after asking Nepal. Since then, India has not removed its army from there under various pretexts and has now started claiming that land as its own.

If we trace the root of the Lipulekh dispute, we have to go back to the Sugauli Treaty of 1816. The modern Kalapani dispute became serious after 1962. Diplomatic disputes between Nepal and India over Lipulekh began in 2015. Only after India released its new map in 2020, including Lipulekh, Kalapani, and Limpiyadhura, did the Nepali government become serious and start showing interest in that territory.

Beginning of the Dispute

According to a former secretary of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, although the Lipulekh dispute is very old, governments during the Panchayat and multiparty eras never took it seriously. Although the Mahakali and Kalapani rivers were raised during surveys from Nepal's side, the issue was never formally raised at the government level. Even though India kept its army there, it did not engage in much activity initially. However, Nepal became alarmed only after an agreement was made to build a road through Nepali territory for trade with China and for pilgrimage to Mansarovar, he said.

The former secretary stated that the main reason India claims that territory as its own is that it has been using that land for a long time. If interest had been shown from the beginning and efforts made to remove the Indian army, the issue would not have reached such a serious stage today.

When the then President of the Nepali Congress, Sushil Koirala, was the Prime Minister, he assigned the task of technically resolving the issues of Lipulekh, Limpiyadhura, and Kalapani through discussions with India to the Survey Department. However, the Survey Department, not wanting to take the blame, sent a letter to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs stating that a committee would be formed at the level of foreign secretaries of both countries for discussions, and the department would only provide technical support. Subsequently, a committee was formed with the Foreign Secretary of Nepal during the visit of Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, but its meeting has not yet been held.

Land Swap

Moreover, the Survey Department also suggested swapping land between the two countries to resolve the dispute. Lipulekh Pass is as important for India as it is strategically less important for Nepal. There may be no better place for Nepal to monitor China than that territory. Therefore, the department suggested leaving that land to India and demanding land from Darjeeling to Bangladesh (Chicken's Neck area) from India in return.

The Survey Department had suggested to the then Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs that Nepal could also consider the option of a land swap if India was willing to do so, as Nepal would also gain access to the sea. However, an official from the department said that no one raised this issue with the Indian side at that time.

Various committees and working groups related to the border are active between Nepal and India, and their meetings are held regularly. Meetings are also being held at the district level, but the meeting of the committee formed to resolve the dispute over Lipulekh, Kalapani, and Limpiyadhura has not been held. Former Director General of the Survey Department, Nagendra Jha, says, 'India has not shown interest in holding the meeting. Even if Nepal makes efforts, India evades it by making various excuses.'

Issues Not Raised in Working Groups

Based on the depth of the rivers, historical documents clearly indicate that Lipulekh, Kalapani, and Limpiyadhura are Nepali territories. However, the dispute has arisen because India is claiming the border based on the rivers changing their course, Jha said. He stated that although there are various committees and mechanisms between the two countries, the issues are not progressing because these working groups have not been given the mandate to discuss Lipulekh.

Informed sources say that the issue has become more controversial recently after Prime Minister Balen stated that not only India but also Nepal has encroached on India's land. They argue that this has made it easier for India to maintain its stance. Similarly, the border dispute has become more complex after Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal stated that the Nepali government does not possess the original copy of the Sugauli Treaty and is searching for it.

However, Ratna Bhandari, who has written a book on the Lipulekh issue, says, 'The absence of the original copy of the Sugauli Treaty does not create problems in discussions; Nepal has sufficient historical evidence based on which it can negotiate strongly with India.'

India-China Agreement and Nepal's Objection

India claims to have been trading with China via Lipulekh Pass since 1954. However, Nepal officially began objecting to this in 1999. Nepal protested after an agreement was reached during the visit of then Indian Foreign Minister Jaswant Singh to China in 1999 to make Lipulekh a common trade route for both countries.

Subsequently, in 2005, China and India also reached a 12-point agreement. In that agreement, titled 'Modalities for the Implementation of Confidence Building Measures in the Military Field Along the Line of Actual Control in the India-China Border Areas,' both sides agreed to expand the mechanism of border meeting points by including Lipulekh/Changla Bhanjyang in the middle sector and Kibithu-Dhamai in the eastern sector. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Nepal protested by sending diplomatic notes to both countries at that time.

During the visit of Chinese President Xi Jinping to India in 2014, an agreement was reached to open a new route for the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra. According to officials from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Nepal did not react much at that time. However, Nepal strongly protested when India and China reached an agreement regarding Lipulekh again during Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit to China in 2015. Then Prime Minister Sushil Koirala sent diplomatic notes to both India and China.

Instead of responding, India included Lipulekh, Kalapani, and Limpiyadhura in its map. Despite widespread protests, India ignored them and inaugurated a road in the area. Subsequently, KP Sharma Oli, who became Prime Minister, unveiled a new map including Lipulekh, Kalapani, and Limpiyadhura, got it passed by parliament, and incorporated it into the constitution.

This created a rift in Nepal-India relations for some time, and the issue of Lipulekh became a matter of public concern. Since then, the issue has been raised during the tenure of every government.

During Indian National Security Advisor Ajit Doval's visit to China in December 2024, an agreement was reached to resume the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra via the Lipulekh route. The 12-point agreement reached during Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi's visit to India on August 18, 2025, also mentioned starting border trade via Lipulekh.

There was significant protest in Nepal regarding this, and the government also sent diplomatic notes to both countries. Both countries have sent their responses, but while the dispute remains unresolved, trade activities continue to move forward.

ओना त दुनू देश ओहि जमीनक अध्ययन आ विवादक समाधान पर सहमत भेल मुदा लिपुलेखक बारे मे किछु नहि कहल गेल अछि जे सबस पैघ विवाद अछि। बैठक मे भाग लेनिहार सर्वेक्षण विभाग क एकटा अधिकारी कहला जे समिति कए लिपुलेख क अध्ययन या चर्चा करबाक जनादेश (अधिकार) तक नहि देल गेल। ओ जानकारी देलनि जे भारत मे भेल दू दिनक बैसार मे दुनू पक्ष एहि मुद्दा पर चर्चा तक नहि केलक।

हुनकऽ अनुसार लिपुलेख बहुत संवेदनशील मुद्दा छै, आरू एकरऽ समाधान बिना उच्च स्तरीय हस्तक्षेप के नै करलऽ जाब॑ सकै छै । ओ कहलनि जे, निचला स्तर के कर्मचारी विवादित लिपुलेख के संबंध मे जोखिम नहि उठाबय चाहैत छथि। ओ चेतावनी देलनि जे जँ एकर समाधान जल्दिये नहि भेल त' ई आओर गंभीर मोड़ ल' सकैत अछि, ओ कहलनि जे, 'हम सभ ई नहि कहि सकैत छी जे काल्हि ओतय दोसर गड़बड़ी नहि होयत, तें जल्द सं जल्द एकर समाधान करब नीक रहत.'

ईहो ‘लिपुलेख विवाद तकनीकी नहि अछि, एकर समाधान राजनीतिक आ कूटनीतिक रूपेँ हेबाक चाही’।

देहरादून बैसार

4 आरू 5 अगस्त क॑ देहरादून म॑ आयोजित संयुक्त कार्यदल केरऽ बैठक म॑ हालांकि लिपुलेख क॑ अनौपचारिक रूप स॑ उठाबै के बात कहलऽ गेलै, लेकिन एकरा प॑ एजेंडा के रूप म॑ चर्चा नै करलऽ गेलै । बल्कि कार्यदल नेपाल-भारत सीमा पर निगरानी आ सख्ती बढ़ेबाक निर्णय लेलक ।

ईहो नेपाल-भारत सीमा पर सख्त निगरानी कएल जाएत

बैठक म॑ दूनू देशऽ के नागरिकऽ के सीमा पार स॑ आवागमन म॑ सुविधा, तेसरऽ देश के नागरिकऽ प॑ निगरानी बढ़ाबै, आपदा प्रबंधन, आरू क्षतिग्रस्त सीमा स्तंभऽ के मरम्मत के बारे म॑ चर्चा करलऽ गेलै । ओना लिपुलेख, लिम्पियाधुरा, आ कालापानी पर कोनो निर्णय नहि भेल ।

सीमा विद्वान रत्न भण्डारी के अनुसार लिपुलेख विवाद आब दुनु देश के बीच राजनीतिक विवाद बनि गेल अछि । हुनकऽ कहना छै कि एकरऽ इस्तेमाल राजनीतिक औजार के रूप म॑ करलऽ जाय रहलऽ छै, ई लेली एकरऽ समाधान म॑ कोय भी रुचि नै दिखाय रहलऽ छै । ओ कहलनि जे, विशेष रूप सं भारत एकर समाधान नहि करय चाहैत अछि, आ नेपाल सेहो पर्याप्त रुचि नहि देखौलक अछि, जाहि कारणे एखन धरि विवादक समाधान नहि भ सकल अछि।'

भण्डारी कहलनि जे, 1962 मे भारत-चीन युद्धक समय (पाठक अनुसार 1966) भारत नेपाल सँ पूछलाक बाद अपन सेना ओतय राखि देलक । तहिया सँ भारत विभिन्न बहाने ओतय सँ अपन सेना नहि हटा देलक आ आब ओहि जमीन केँ अपन दावा करय लागल अछि।

अगर लिपुलेख विवाद के जड़ के पता लगाबी त 1816 के सुगौली संधि में वापस जाय पड़त।आधुनिक कलापानी विवाद 1962 के बाद गंभीर भ गेल।लिपुलेख के ल क नेपाल आ भारत के बीच कूटनीतिक विवाद 2015 में शुरू भेल।भारत 2020 में अपन नव नक्शा जारी केलाक बाद मात्र, जाहि में लिपुलेख, कालापानी, आ लिम्पियाधुरा, की नेपाली सरकार गंभीर भ' ओहि इलाका मे रुचि देखाबय लागल.

विवाद के शुरुआत

विदेश मंत्रालय क एकटा पूर्व सचिव क अनुसार लिपुलेख विवाद भले बहुत पुरान अछि, मुदा पंचायत आ बहुदलीय युग मे सरकार एकरा कहियो गंभीरता स नहि लेलक। ओना नेपाल दिस स सर्वेक्षण क दौरान महाकाली आ कालापानी नदी उठल मुदा सरकारी स्तर पर कहियो औपचारिक रूप स इ मुद्दा नहि उठल। भारत अपन सेना ओतहि राखि लेलक मुदा शुरू मे बेसी गतिविधि नहि केलक । मुदा चीन के संग व्यापार आ मनसरोवर के तीर्थयात्रा के लेल नेपाली इलाका स सड़क बनेबाक समझौता भेलाक बाद नेपाल घबरा गेल ओ कहलनि।

पूर्व सचिव के कहनाय छनि जे भारत ओहि इलाका के अपन दावा करय के मुख्य कारण ई अछि जे ओ ओहि जमीन के बहुत दिन सं उपयोग क रहल अछि. अगर शुरूए स रुचि देखाउल गेल रहैत आ भारतीय सेना कए हटाबय क प्रयास कैल जाइत त आइ इ मुद्दा एतेक गंभीर अवस्था मे नहि पहुंचल रहैत।

नेपाली कांग्रेसक तत्कालीन अध्यक्ष सुशील कोइराला जखन प्रधानमंत्री छलाह तखन भारतक संग चर्चाक माध्यमे लिपुलेख, लिम्पियाधुरा, आ कालापानीक मुद्दा केँ तकनीकी रूप सँ समाधान करबाक काज सर्वेक्षण विभाग केँ देलनि । लेकिन सर्वेक्षण विभाग एकरऽ दोष नै लेबै चाहला स॑ विदेश मंत्रालय क॑ एगो चिट्ठी भेजलकै जेकरा म॑ कहलऽ गेलऽ छेलै कि चर्चा लेली दोनों देशऽ के विदेश सचिवऽ के स्तर प॑ एगो समिति के गठन करलऽ जैतै, आरू विभाग खाली तकनीकी सहायता देतै । तत्पश्चात भारतीय प्रधानमन्त्री नरेन्द्र मोदीक यात्रामे नेपालक विदेश सचिवक संग समिति गठन कएल गेल, मुदा ओकर बैसार एखन धरि नहि भेल अछि ।

भूमि अदला-बदली

एतबे नहि सर्वेक्षण विभाग एहि विवाद क समाधान लेल दुनू देश क बीच जमीन क अदला-बदली क सेहो सुझाव देलक। लिपुलेख दर्रा भारत के लेल ओतबे महत्वपूर्ण अछि जतेक नेपाल के लेल सामरिक रूप स कम। चीन पर नजरि रखबा लेल नेपाल लेल ओहि इलाका स नीक कोनो जगह नहि भ सकैत अछि। एहि लेल विभाग ओ जमीन भारत पर छोड़बाक आ बदला मे भारत स दार्जिलिंग स बांग्लादेश (चिकन नेक एरिया) क जमीन मांगबाक सुझाव देलक।

सर्वेक्षण विभाग तत्कालीन प्रधानमंत्री आ विदेश मंत्री कए सुझाव देने छल जे भारत इच्छुक रहला पर नेपाल सेहो भूमि अदला-बदली क विकल्प पर विचार क सकैत अछि, किया कि नेपाल कए सेहो समुद्र तक पहुंच भेटत। ओना विभाग क एकटा अधिकारी कहला जे ओहि समय भारतीय पक्ष स इ मुद्दा कियो नहि उठेलक।

नेपाल आ भारत के बीच सीमा स संबंधित विभिन्न समिति आ कार्यदल सक्रिय अछि, आ ओकर बैसार नियमित रूप स होइत अछि । जिला स्तर पर सेहो बैसार भ रहल अछि, मुदा लिपुलेख, कालापानी, आ लिम्पियाधुरा के विवाद सुलझाबय लेल बनल समिति के बैसार नहि भेल अछि. सर्वेक्षण विभागक पूर्व महानिदेशक नागेन्द्र झा कहैत छथि, ‘भारत एहि बैसार करबा मे रुचि नहि देखौलक अछि। नेपाल प्रयास करै तबो भारत विभिन्न बहाना बना कऽ टालैत अछि ।'

कार्यदल मे नहि उठल मुद्दा

नदी सब के गहराई के आधार पर ऐतिहासिक दस्तावेज स स्पष्ट संकेत भेटैत अछि जे लिपुलेख, कालापानी, आ लिम्पियाधुरा नेपाली क्षेत्र अछि | ओना विवाद एहि लेल उठल अछि जे भारत नदी क रस्ता बदलबाक आधार पर सीमा पर दावा क रहल अछि, झा कहला। हुनी कहलकै कि हालांकि दूनू देश के बीच विभिन्न समिति आरू तंत्र छै, लेकिन मुद्दा आगू नै बढ़ी रहलौ छै, कैन्हेंकि ई कार्यदल क लिपुलेख प चर्चा करै के जनादेश नै देलऽ गेलऽ छै ।

सूचित सूत्रक कहब अछि जे, प्रधानमंत्री बालेन भारते नहि, नेपाल सेहो भारतक जमीन पर अतिक्रमण केने कहला के बाद हाल मे ई मुद्दा बेसी विवादित भ गेल अछि। हुनकऽ तर्क छै कि एकरा स॑ भारत क॑ अपनऽ रुख कायम रखै म॑ आसानी होय गेलऽ छै । तहिना विदेश मंत्री शिशिर खनाल नेपाली सरकार लग सुगौली संधिक मूल प्रति नहि अछि आ ओकर खोज मे लागल अछि से कहला के बाद सीमा विवाद आओर जटिल भ गेल अछि ।

मुदा, लिपुलेख मुद्दा पर पोथी लिखनिहार रत्न भण्डारी कहैत छथि, 'सुगौली संधिक मूल प्रतिक अभाव मे चर्चा मे समस्या नहि उत्पन्न होइत छैक; नेपाल के पास पर्याप्त ऐतिहासिक प्रमाण छै, जेकरा आधार पर भारत के साथ मजबूती स॑ बातचीत करी सकै छै ।'

भारत-चीन सम्झौता आ नेपालक आपत्ति

भारत के दावा छै कि चीन के साथ लिपुलेख दर्रा के माध्यम स॑ १९५४ स॑ व्यापार करी रहलऽ छै ।मुदा नेपाल न॑ आधिकारिक तौर प॑ १९९९ म॑ एकरा प॑ आपत्ति करना शुरू करी देलकै ।१९९९ म॑ तत्कालीन भारतीय विदेश मंत्री जसवंत सिंह केरऽ चीन यात्रा के दौरान लिपुलेख क॑ दूनू देश लेली साझा व्यापारिक मार्ग बनाबै के समझौता होय के बाद नेपाल न॑ एकरऽ विरोध करलकै ।

एकरऽ बाद २००५ म॑ चीन आरू भारत के बीच भी १२ सूत्री समझौता होय गेलै । ‘भारत-चीन सीमा क्षेत्रऽ म॑ वास्तविक नियंत्रण के रेखा के साथ सैन्य क्षेत्र म॑ विश्वास निर्माण के उपायऽ के कार्यान्वयन के तरीका’ शीर्षक स॑ बनलऽ वू समझौता म॑ दूनू पक्ष न॑ मध्य क्षेत्र म॑ लिपुलेख/चांगला भंजयांग आरू पूर्वी क्षेत्र म॑ किबिथु-धमाई क॑ शामिल करी क॑ सीमा बैठक बिंदु के तंत्र क॑ विस्तारित करै प॑ सहमत होय गेलै । नेपालक विदेश मन्त्रालय ओहि समय दुनू देश मे कूटनीतिक नोट पठा क विरोध केलक ।

2014 में चीन के राष्ट्रपति शी जिनपिंग के भारत यात्रा के दौरान कैलाश मनसरोवर यात्रा के लेल एकटा नव मार्ग खोलय के समझौता भेल छल. विदेश मंत्रालय के अधिकारी के अनुसार ओहि समय नेपाल मे कोनो खास प्रतिक्रिया नहि छल. मुदा २०१५ मे प्रधानमन्त्री नरेन्द्र मोदीक चीन यात्राक क्रममे भारत आ चीन पुनः लिपुलेखक संबंधमे सहमति भेला पर नेपाल कड़ा विरोध केलक ।तखन प्रधानमन्त्री सुशील कोइराला भारत आ चीन दुनू दिस कूटनीतिक नोट पठौलनि ।

भारत प्रतिक्रिया देबाक बदला अपन नक्शा मे लिपुलेख, कालापानी, आ लिम्पियाधुरा के शामिल केलक । व्यापक विरोध के बावजूद भारत हुनका सब के अनदेखी क एहि इलाका मे एकटा सड़क के उद्घाटन केलक। एकरऽ बाद प्रधानमंत्री बनला केपी शर्मा ओली न॑ लिपुलेख, कालापानी, आरू लिम्पियाधुरा सहित एगो नया नक्शा के अनावरण करी क॑ संसद स॑ पारित करी क॑ संविधान म॑ शामिल करी लेलकै ।

एहि सँ नेपाल-भारत संबंध मे किछु समय धरि दरार उत्पन्न भेल, आ लिपुलेखक मुद्दा जनसरोकारक विषय बनि गेल । तहिया स इ मुद्दा हर सरकार क कार्यकाल मे उठल अछि।

दिसंबर २०२४ म॑ भारतीय राष्ट्रीय सुरक्षा सलाहकार अजीत डोवल केरऽ चीन यात्रा के दौरान लिपुलेख मार्ग के माध्यम स॑ कैलाश मनसरोवर यात्रा क॑ फेर स॑ शुरू करै के समझौता होय गेलऽ छेलै । चीन केरऽ विदेश मंत्री वांग यी केरऽ १८ अगस्त २०२५ क॑ भारत यात्रा के दौरान करलऽ गेलऽ १२ सूत्री समझौता म॑ लिपुलेख के माध्यम स॑ सीमा व्यापार शुरू करै के भी जिक्र करलऽ गेलऽ छै ।

एहि संबंध मे नेपाल मे काफी विरोध भेल, आ सरकार दुनू देश कए कूटनीतिक नोट सेहो पठेलक । दुनू देश अपन प्रतिक्रिया पठौने अछि, मुदा विवाद जखन कि अनसुलझल अछि, व्यापारिक गतिविधि आगू बढ़ैत अछि।

The inaugural edition of the NVL, organised by Kedia Group, will be held from September 4 to 12.

Kathmandu, Aug 24: The House of Representatives (HoR) of the Federal Parliament is scheduled to meet today at 1:00 pm, where the relevant ministers will respond to the quires of lawmakers.

Finance Minister Dr. Swarnim Wagle, on behalf of the Prime Minister Balendra Shah, is anticipated to propose forwarding the First Amendment Bill, 2083, which addresses the remuneration and services of constitutional office bearers, to the appropriate committee for further examination.

Additionally, Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal will present a proposal to send the Passport (First Amendment) Bill, 2083, to the relevant committee for in-depth discussion.

Minister Sita Badi will also propose that the Human Trafficking and Transportation (Control) (First Amendment) Bill, 2083, be sent for further deliberation, while Minister Gauri Kumari is expected to propose sending the Mines and Minerals Bill, 2083, to the relevant committee.

Meanwhile, five parliamentary committees are meeting today: International Relations and Tourism, Agriculture and Natural Resources, Infrastructure Development, Legislative Management, and Public Policy and Delegated Legislation.(RSS)

title: 'His feet are his pillars': Nepal para swimmer gives all for Asian glory - Yahoo Sports
description: 'His feet are his pillars': Nepal para swimmer gives all for Asian glory  Yahoo Sports
publisher.title: Yahoo Sports
full_article:
Every morning Harka Man Gharti slices into the blue water of a swimming pool in Nepal's capital Kathmandu, chasing a dream that stretches far beyond its 25 metres.

Unlike the swimmers around him who rely on long strokes of their arms, Gharti powers through his legs and torso because he does not have arms.

The 21-year-old is training with three other disabled swimmers who will represent Nepal in the Asian Para Games in Japan in October, chasing medals despite limited resources in the Himalayan country.

"It is not my hope, it is my target," Gharti told AFP after finishing a gruelling session. "Just for a medal, I am giving everything... every possible thing."

A decade ago an electrocution accident near a hydroelectric project in his native Baglung district in western Nepal changed his life forever, costing him both arms.

The tragedy that could have ended his ambitions instead helped forge his extraordinary determination.

What began as an experiment with competitive swimming in 2020 soon became a passion and a career pathway.

"I love everything about swimming, whether competitive or just for enjoying," he said.

At the hostel where he lives in Kathmandu a row of medals hangs above his bed, proof of a remarkable journey.

During training he concentrates on his technique and body position in the water. On race days a different instinct takes over.

"I don't really think about the techniques or my body alignment," he said. "I just go hard. I just push fast and I just want to push power. That's it. I just think about speed and for speed I just kick harder and harder."

- Leg power -

At last year's Para Swimming World Series in Japan, Gharti's times met the minimum qualifying standards for the Asian Para Games, earning him a chance to compete on one of the biggest sporting stages.

He will participate in the S5 classification, including the 50-metre freestyle.

China's Guo Jincheng holds the men's 50m freestyle record at 29.33 seconds in the category.

Sports facilities in Nepal are modest by international standards.

Para athletes in the country often face limited funding, scarce specialised infrastructure and a lack of competitive opportunities.

His coach, Subha Shrestha, believes Gharti's greatest strength lies not in what he has lost, but in what he has built.

"When we don't have even a single finger we feel the impact," Shrestha said. "But he is working so hard with no hands.

"His feet are his pillars, his legs are very powerful."

The wider significance of Gharti's quest is not lost on Nepal's para swimming community.

The nation has had only one Asian Para Games medallist, taekwondo athlete Palesha Goverdhan, who won bronze last time out before also claiming a medal in Paralympics.

For many years Nepali athletes have arrived at major competitions with modest expectations.

"In Nepal they often say that we go only for the sake of participation," said Saroj Shrestha, president of the National Para Swimming Association of Nepal.

"But Harka and we both dream to do something in swimming that even able-bodied athletes have not been able to achieve."

- Inspiring others -

Back on the pool deck, Gharti's ambitions extend beyond sport.

Having recently completed high school, he plans to study computer science.

He navigates a computer with his toes, displaying the same determination that has become central to his swimming.

"Swimming is a platform for me where it is on me whether I can make my life better or not.

"Because if I hit a world record then of course my life will be better," he said.

"Only then can I speak of inspiring anyone else."

एकटा थकाऊ सत्र समाप्त केलाक बाद घरती एएफपी स कहलथि जे इ हमर उम्मीद नहि अछि, इ हमर निशाना अछि। "बस मेडल लेल हम सब किछु द' रहल छी... हर संभव चीज."

जे 2020 में प्रतिस्पर्धी तैराकी के प्रयोग के रूप में शुरू भेल छल ओ जल्दिये एकटा पैशन आ कैरियर के मार्ग बनि गेल।

ओ 50 मीटर फ्रीस्टाइल सहित एस 5 वर्गीकरण मे भाग लेताह।

चीन केरऽ गुओ जिनचेंग केरऽ पुरुष ५० मीटर फ्रीस्टाइल केरऽ रिकॉर्ड २९.३३ सेकंड के साथ छै ।

नेपालमे खेलक सुविधा अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय मानकसँ मामूली अछि ।

देश म॑ पैरा एथलीटऽ क॑ अक्सर सीमित फंडिंग, दुर्लभ विशेष बुनियादी ढाँचा आरू प्रतिस्पर्धी अवसरऽ के कमी के सामना करना पड़ै छै ।

हुनकऽ कोच सुभा श्रेष्ठ के मानना ​​छै कि घरती केरऽ सबस॑ बड़ऽ ताकत वू चीज म॑ नै छै, बल्कि ओकरऽ निर्माण म॑ छै ।

श्रेष्ठ कहलनि जे, जखन हमरा सब लग एको आँगुर तक नहि रहैत अछि त एकर असर महसूस होइत अछि। "मुदा ओ एतेक मेहनति क' रहल छथि जे हाथ नहि अछि."

"पएर ओकर खंभा छै, टांग बहुत शक्तिशाली छै।"

घरती के खोज के व्यापक महत्व नेपाल के पैरा तैराकी समुदाय पर नै हेराय छै ।

राष्ट्र के पास एशियाई पैरा गेम्स केरऽ खाली एगो पदक विजेता ताइक्वांडो एथलीट पलेशा गोवर्धन रहलऽ छै, जे पैरालिम्पिक म॑ भी पदक प॑ दावा करै स॑ पहल॑ पिछला बार आउट होय क॑ कांस्य पदक जीतल॑ छेलै ।

कतेको वर्ष सँ नेपाली एथलीट मामूली अपेक्षाक संग पैघ प्रतियोगिता मे पहुँचैत छथि ।

नेपालक राष्ट्रिय पारा तैराकी संघके अध्यक्ष सरोज श्रेष्ठ कहलनि जे, नेपालमे ओ सब प्रायः कहैत छथि जे हम सब मात्र सहभागिता लेल जाइत छी ।

"मुदा हरका आरू हम्में दोनों के सपना छै कि तैराकी में कुछ ऐसनऽ करलौ जाय जेकरा सक्षम एथलीट भी नै हासिल करी सकलऽ छै।"

- दोसरो के प्रेरित करब -

पूल डेक पर वापसी मे घरती क महत्वाकांक्षा खेल स आगू बढ़ि गेल अछि।

हालहि मे हाई स्कूल पूरा केलाक बाद हुनकर योजना कंप्यूटर साइंस के पढ़ाई करय के अछि.

ओ अपन पैरक आँगुरसँ कंप्यूटरकेँ नेविगेट करैत छथि , ओहि दृढ़ संकल्पकेँ प्रदर्शित करैत छथि जे हुनकर हेलबामे केंद्रीय बनि गेल अछि ।

"तैराकी हमरा लेल एकटा एहन मंच अछि जतय ई हमरा पर अछि जे हम अपन जीवन केँ नीक बना सकब वा नहि।"

full_article:
Kathmandu, August 24

Nepal imported paddy and rice worth nearly Rs 1.8 billion in the first month of the current fiscal year 2082/83 BS.

According to data from the Department of Customs, Nepal imported 24,939 tonnes of paddy and rice worth Rs 1.78 billion in Shrawan, the first month of the fiscal year. The imports amounted to 24.94 million kilograms. Paddy and rice imports declined compared to the same month last fiscal year. In Shrawan of fiscal year 2081/82 BS, Nepal imported 57,083 tonnes of paddy and rice worth Rs 2.93 billion.

The data shows a decline in both the volume of imports and the amount spent on them during the first month of the current fiscal year compared to the corresponding period last year. A breakdown of the imports shows that the largest amount was spent on rice. In Shrawan, Nepal imported 11,852 tonnes of rice worth Rs 833.32 million. Almost the entire quantity—11,851 tonnes—was imported from neighbouring India, while a negligible 0.24 tonnes (240 kg) came from Italy.

Basmati rice ranked second in terms of import value. Nepal imported 4,125 tonnes of Basmati rice worth Rs 568.59 million in Shrawan, all of which came from India. In addition to milled rice, Nepal also imports a significant quantity of unmilled paddy. In the first month of the current fiscal year, 8,628 tonnes of paddy worth Rs 365.02 million were imported, all from India.

Similarly, Nepal spent millions of rupees importing broken rice. In Shrawan alone, 332 tonnes of broken rice worth Rs 13.31 million were imported from India. The customs data also shows that small quantities of brown rice and paddy seeds were imported, in addition to the larger volumes of paddy, rice and broken rice.

Nepal imported 625 kg of brown rice worth Rs 89,000 in Shrawan, of which 500 kg came from Thailand and 125 kg from India. Likewise, 67 kg of paddy seeds worth Rs 501,000 were imported during the first month of the current fiscal year. More paddy seeds were imported from China than from India.

In Brief:

Tiger population up 73% in Parsa, from 41 in 2022 to 71 in 2026

Park begins CA|TS certification process to strengthen conservation

Workshop held with officials, partners, security agencies and communities

Focus on habitat, prey, anti-poaching, coexistence and long-term safety

Parsa National Park's tiger population has risen by nearly 73 per cent in four years, prompting the park to begin a process to bring its conservation management in line with international standards.

Related Articles JICA Chief, Dr Tanaka Akihiko, reaffirms Japan's long-term Development Commitment to Nepal Nepal's tiger population climbs to 429, nearly quadrupling since 2010

The number of adult tigers in the park increased from 41 in 2022 to 71 in the 2026 census. Authorities have now initiated the Conservation Assured | Tiger Standards (CA|TS) certification process to turn the population gain into long-term and quality conservation.

A CA|TS workshop organised by the Department of National Parks and Wildlife Conservation was recently held at Parsa, bringing together officials, conservation partners, security agencies, park staff, buffer-zone representatives and local stakeholders.

Park Chief Conservation Officer Ram Chandra Khatiwada said the workshop discussed initial preparations, self-assessment, management improvements, evidence collection and coordination among stakeholders.

Senior ecologist Haribhadhra Acharya said the rise in tiger numbers alone was not enough to ensure long-term conservation.

He said sustained improvement in habitat, prey availability, security and overall management was necessary, adding that CA|TS would assess the broader conservation management system against international standards rather than simply counting tigers.

Khatiwada said the increase in tiger numbers was an important conservation achievement, but the park now faced the challenge of keeping both tigers and local communities safe.

He said the park's 'Tiger Friend Campaign' could be linked with the CA|TS process to strengthen awareness, community participation and human-tiger coexistence.

The certification process will assess habitat and prey protection, anti-poaching measures, smart patrolling, scientific monitoring, community participation, human-tiger conflict, tourism and the long-term status of tigers.

The process will involve registration, self-assessment, preparation of improvement plans and compliance documents, national review, independent assessment and an international decision.

Stakeholders at the workshop stressed that CA|TS should not be treated merely as a process to obtain certification, but as a joint initiative involving the park, buffer-zone communities, security agencies, conservation partners and local residents.

Authorities expect the process to make Parsa's conservation management more scientific, systematic and consistent with international standards. Khatiwada said the ultimate measure of conservation success would be tigers remaining safe, forests remaining healthy and local communities becoming secure and active partners in conservation, rather than the certificate itself.

title: 'His feet are his pillars': Nepal para swimmer gives all for Asian glory - Bangladesh Sangbad Sangstha (BSS)

publisher.title: Bangladesh Sangbad Sangstha (BSS)

KATHMANDU, Nepal, Aug 24, 2026 (BSS/AFP) - Every morning Harka Man Gharti slices into the blue water of a swimming pool in Nepal's capital Kathmandu, chasing a dream that stretches far beyond its 25 metres.

Unlike the swimmers around him who rely on long strokes of their arms, Gharti powers through his legs and torso because he does not have arms.

The 21-year-old is training with three other disabled swimmers who will represent Nepal in the Asian Para Games in Japan in October, chasing medals despite limited resources in the Himalayan country.

"It is not my hope, it is my target," Gharti told AFP after finishing a gruelling session. "Just for a medal, I am giving everything... every possible thing."

A decade ago an electrocution accident near a hydroelectric project in his native Baglung district in western Nepal changed his life forever, costing him both arms.

The tragedy that could have ended his ambitions instead helped forge his extraordinary determination.

What began as an experiment with competitive swimming in 2020 soon became a passion and a career pathway.

"I love everything about swimming, whether competitive or just for enjoying," he said.

At the hostel where he lives in Kathmandu a row of medals hangs above his bed, proof of a remarkable journey.

During training he concentrates on his technique and body position in the water. On race days a different instinct takes over.

"I don't really think about the techniques or my body alignment," he said. "I just go hard. I just push fast and I just want to push power. That's it. I just think about speed and for speed I just kick harder and harder."

- Leg power -

At last year's Para Swimming World Series in Japan, Gharti's times met the minimum qualifying standards for the Asian Para Games, earning him a chance to compete on one of the biggest sporting stages.

He will participate in the S5 classification, including the 50-metre freestyle.

China's Guo Jincheng holds the men's 50m freestyle record at 29.33 seconds in the category.

Sports facilities in Nepal are modest by international standards.

Para athletes in the country often face limited funding, scarce specialised infrastructure and a lack of competitive opportunities.

His coach, Subha Shrestha, believes Gharti's greatest strength lies not in what he has lost, but in what he has built.

"When we don't have even a single finger we feel the impact," Shrestha said. "But he is working so hard with no hands.

"His feet are his pillars, his legs are very powerful."

The wider significance of Gharti's quest is not lost on Nepal's para swimming community.

The nation has had only one Asian Para Games medallist, taekwondo athlete Palesha Goverdhan, who won bronze last time out before also claiming a medal in Paralympics.

For many years Nepali athletes have arrived at major competitions with modest expectations.

"In Nepal they often say that we go only for the sake of participation," said Saroj Shrestha, president of the National Para Swimming Association of Nepal.

"But Harka and we both dream to do something in swimming that even able-bodied athletes have not been able to achieve."

- Inspiring others -

Back on the pool deck, Gharti's ambitions extend beyond sport.

Having recently completed high school, he plans to study computer science.

He navigates a computer with his toes, displaying the same determination that has become central to his swimming.

"Swimming is a platform for me where it is on me whether I can make my life better or not.

"Because if I hit a world record then of course my life will be better," he said.

"Only then can I speak of inspiring anyone else."

काठमांडू मे जाहि हॉस्टल मे ओ रहैत छथि ओहि मे हुनकर पलंग क ऊपर पदक क पंक्ति लटकल अछि जे एकटा उल्लेखनीय यात्रा क प्रमाण अछि ।

प्रशिक्षण के दौरान ओ अपन तकनीक आ पानि मे शरीर के स्थिति पर ध्यान केंद्रित करैत छथि । दौड़क दिन एकटा अलग वृत्ति अपन कब्जा जमा लैत अछि ।

ओ कहलनि जे, हम वास्तव मे तकनीक या अपन शरीर के संरेखण के बारे मे नहि सोचैत छी। "हम त' बस जोर सँ जाइत छी. हम त' बस तेजी सँ धक्का दैत छी आओर हम बस पावर केँ धक्का देब' चाहैत छी. एतबे। हम त' बस गति'क बारे मे सोचैत छी आओर गति'क लेल हम बस जोर सँ आओर जोर सँ लात मारैत छी."

पिछला साल जापान म॑ आयोजित पैरा तैराकी वर्ल्ड सीरीज म॑ घरती केरऽ समय एशियाई पैरा गेम्स लेली न्यूनतम क्वालीफाइंग मानक क॑ पूरा करी क॑ हुनका एगो बड़ऽ खेल मंच प॑ प्रतिस्पर्धा करै के मौका मिललै ।

ओ 50 मीटर फ्रीस्टाइल सहित एस 5 वर्गीकरण मे भाग लेताह।

चीन केरऽ गुओ जिनचेंग केरऽ पुरुष ५० मीटर फ्रीस्टाइल केरऽ रिकॉर्ड २९.३३ सेकंड के साथ छै ।

नेपालमे खेलक सुविधा अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय मानकसँ मामूली अछि ।

देश म॑ पैरा एथलीटऽ क॑ अक्सर सीमित फंडिंग, दुर्लभ विशेष बुनियादी ढाँचा आरू प्रतिस्पर्धी अवसरऽ के कमी के सामना करना पड़ै छै ।

हुनकऽ कोच सुभा श्रेष्ठ के मानना ​​छै कि घरती केरऽ सबस॑ बड़ऽ ताकत वू चीज म॑ नै छै, बल्कि ओकरऽ निर्माण म॑ छै ।

श्रेष्ठ कहलनि जे, जखन हमरा सब लग एको आँगुर तक नहि रहैत अछि त एकर असर महसूस होइत अछि। "मुदा ओ एतेक मेहनति क' रहल छथि जे हाथ नहि अछि."

"पएर ओकर खंभा छै, टांग बहुत शक्तिशाली छै।"

घरती के खोज के व्यापक महत्व नेपाल के पैरा तैराकी समुदाय पर नै हेराय छै ।

राष्ट्र के पास एशियाई पैरा गेम्स केरऽ खाली एगो पदक विजेता ताइक्वांडो एथलीट पलेशा गोवर्धन रहलऽ छै, जे पैरालिम्पिक म॑ भी पदक प॑ दावा करै स॑ पहल॑ पिछला बार आउट होय क॑ कांस्य पदक जीतल॑ छेलै ।

कतेको वर्ष सँ नेपाली एथलीट मामूली अपेक्षाक संग पैघ प्रतियोगिता मे पहुँचैत छथि ।

नेपालक राष्ट्रिय पारा तैराकी संघके अध्यक्ष सरोज श्रेष्ठ कहलनि जे, नेपालमे ओ सब प्रायः कहैत छथि जे हम सब मात्र सहभागिता लेल जाइत छी ।

"मुदा हरका आरू हम्में दोनों के सपना छै कि तैराकी में कुछ ऐसनऽ करलौ जाय जेकरा सक्षम एथलीट भी नै हासिल करी सकलऽ छै।"

- दोसरो के प्रेरित करब -

पूल डेक पर वापसी मे घरती क महत्वाकांक्षा खेल स आगू बढ़ि गेल अछि।

हालहि मे हाई स्कूल पूरा केलाक बाद हुनकर योजना कंप्यूटर साइंस के पढ़ाई करय के अछि.

ओ अपन पैरक आँगुरसँ कंप्यूटरकेँ नेविगेट करैत छथि , ओहि दृढ़ संकल्पकेँ प्रदर्शित करैत छथि जे हुनकर हेलबामे केंद्रीय बनि गेल अछि ।

"तैराकी हमरा लेल एकटा एहन मंच अछि जतय ई हमरा पर अछि जे हम अपन जीवन केँ नीक बना सकब वा नहि।"

ओ कहलनि जे, कारण जौं हम विश्व रिकॉर्ड बना लेब तखन बेशक हमर जीवन नीक भ जायत।

description: NDTV World to hold India-Nepal dialogue in Kathmandu  The Kathmandu Post
publisher.title: The Kathmandu Post
full_article:
NDTV World is set to launch “NDTV Anviksha: Ideas Across Borders”, a global conversation series aimed at creating a deeper understanding between countries by allowing them to articulate their own ideas, ambitions, anxieties and perspectives.

The inaugural edition, “The India-Nepal Dialogue”, will be held in Kathmandu on Thursday, bringing together political leaders, policymakers, diplomats, business leaders, strategic thinkers and cultural figures from Nepal and India.

Kantipur Media Group will be the Nepal media partner for the initiative, bringing together the reach of two major South Asian media organisations. Kantipur TV will broadcast the event to audiences in Nepal.

According to NDTV, the initiative seeks to move beyond familiar narratives and assumptions about countries by creating conversations rooted in inquiry, reflection and listening. The name Anviksha draws from the ancient Indian tradition of “anvīkṣikī”, which refers to the pursuit of understanding through reason, reflection and examination.

The series will travel across countries, placing a nation at the centre of each edition and examining its history, identity, lived realities and ambitions alongside broader geopolitical and economic developments.

The Nepal dialogue comes as the country undergoes political, economic and social changes while seeking to define its place in a changing Asian and global order. The discussions will explore Nepal’s economic ambitions, entrepreneurial activity, democratic evolution and the aspirations of its young population, as well as opportunities in technology, tourism, infrastructure, sustainability, trade and regional cooperation.

ई श्रृंखला देशऽ के यात्रा करतै, जेकरा म॑ हर संस्करण के केंद्र म॑ एगो राष्ट्र क॑ रखलऽ जैतै आरू एकरऽ इतिहास, पहचान, जीवित वास्तविकता आरू महत्वाकांक्षा के साथ-साथ व्यापक भू-राजनीतिक आरू आर्थिक विकास के जांच करलऽ जैतै ।

नेपाल केरऽ संवाद ऐन्हऽ समय म॑ आबी रहलऽ छै जब॑ देश म॑ बदलतऽ एशियाई आरू वैश्विक व्यवस्था म॑ अपनऽ स्थान परिभाषित करै के कोशिश करलऽ जाय रहलऽ छै । एहि चर्चा मे नेपालक आर्थिक महत्वाकांक्षा, उद्यमशीलताक गतिविधि, लोकतांत्रिक विकास आ ओकर युवा आबादी केर आकांक्षाक संग-संग प्रौद्योगिकी, पर्यटन, बुनियादी ढांचा, स्थायित्व, व्यापार आ क्षेत्रीय सहयोग मे अवसरक खोज होयत।
